newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS - EU clears Baxter taking Immuno.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - EU clears Baxter taking Immuno.

text.p: The European Commission cleared on Thursday the acquisition of Swiss-based Immuno International AG by Baxter International of the United States, creating a global blood-products supplier.

It said in a statement that the two companies' combined share of the European market for plasma-derived products would be less than 30 percent. It could be higher in some unspecified national markets, namely for products used in the treatment of haemophiliac bleeding.
But hospitals specialised in the treatment of haemophilia had not raised any objections.
"Hospitals have not expressed concerns about the proposed concentration, which is generally viewed as enhancing competition in the plasma derivatives markets," the Commission said.
The deal, announced by the companies at the end of August, is to create a leading blood plasma company, a field in which Immuno is a strong European player.
Immuno, whose main operations are in Austria, also makes vaccines, while Baxter also develops and markets products for heart and vascular diseases and renal care products.
The Commission is the clearing house for all major mergers and takeovers that affect trade in the European Union.

In clearing Baxter's takeover of Immuno, it took into consideration the existence of several competitors in the same market. They include Centeon, a joint venture between German group Hoechst and France's Rhone-Poulenc-Rorer, Bayer and Pharmacia/Upjohn.
